descripcion_geo: Narrow sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. In the AT, the 'Yam Suf' (Sea of ​​Reeds), scene of the miraculous passage of the exodus.
importancia_estrategica: Natural border between Egypt and Arabia; scene of the founding miracle of the town of Israel.

historias.titulo: The miraculous passage of the Red Sea
historias.descripcion: Moses extends the rod and the sea is divided; Israel crosses on dry land while the Egyptian army perishes in the waters.

historias.titulo: The song of Moses and Miriam
historias.descripcion: After the passage of the sea, Moses sings the song of victory and Miriam dances with tambourines celebrating the salvation of the Lord.

historias.titulo: The Red Sea in the NT: type of baptism
historias.descripcion: Paul interprets the crossing of the Red Sea as a type of Christian baptism: all were 'baptized in Moses in the sea'.

personajes.descripcion: He stretched out the rod over the sea; his faith at the most critical moment saved the entire Israel.
She led the Israelite women's victory song after the passage of the sea.
His army pursued Israel into the sea and he perished in the waters.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: The Red Sea is the setting for Israel's founding event: the exodus. His miraculous step is cited throughout the Bible as a paradigm of divine salvation.

mitos.nombre: The passage of the Red Sea

judaismo.descripcion: The crossing of the Red Sea is the founding event of the people of God: birth of Israel as a free nation.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The crossing of the Red Sea is the founding event of the people of God: birth of Israel as a free nation.

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: Paul interprets it as a type of Christian baptism (1 Cor 10:1-2); Hebrews cites it as an act of faith (Heb 11:29).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Paul interprets it as a type of Christian baptism (1 Cor 10:1-2); Hebrews cites it as an act of faith (Heb 11:29).
